reasons.figures_tables: Paper A has few figures, and they mostly display missing cells and 'missing 3/3' annotations (p5-6); Paper B has a consistent style across many figures and clean booktabs tables (p4, p7, p14-28), though some plots have large empty areas (p5c).
reasons.experiments: Paper A retains only 5 of 9 planned cells, has no width-256 final data and reports that its final evaluation 'failed scientific qualification' (p1, p4), so it cannot support its claim; Paper B runs 204 registered runs over five widths with 12 seeds, bootstrap and Wilson intervals, frozen-feature, decay, learning-rate, split and operation controls, and threshold sensitivities (p4-7, p21-22).
reasons.page_use: Both bodies run about 8 pages with only 7-8 references (A p9, B p9); Paper B's large appendix and checklist add no body content, but its body is denser with results.
reasons.clean_text: Paper A's body is mostly clean, but its appendix is full of script paths, SHA-256 hashes and tool talk (p10-12); Paper B likewise puts file paths and run IDs such as decay_w512_b04 in its appendix (p11-13), with only a brief mention of agents in the body (p8).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract and introduction dwell on missing records and failed qualification, which reads as a defensive pipeline report (p1); Paper B's abstract states a testable explanation and three falsifiable predictions (P1-P3) with their outcomes, and flows better as a NeurIPS paper (p1-3).

reasons.figures_tables: Paper A has a consistent grayscale figure style and clean booktabs tables across pages 4–28, if very dense; Paper B's few figures and tables (pages 4–7) are clean but sparse and contain 'missing' annotations.
reasons.experiments: Paper A reports 204 runs over 5 widths with 12 paired seeds, plus frozen-feature, decay, learning-rate, orbit-split and multiplication controls and threshold sensitivities (pages 4–7); Paper B has only 5 of 9 planned cells, no widest-width final data and a failed final qualification (page 4), so it cannot support its claims.
reasons.page_use: Both bodies run to about 8 pages, but Paper A fills its pages with substantive results, while Paper B spends much of pages 4–8 explaining missing data and caveats.
